A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TEFormer work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–B support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, encoding comparisons, and component ablations. Appendix B also reports original SVHN and model-size results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds gate comparisons, computational and estimated-energy results, and temporal-enhancement-depth experiments in Tables 7, 9, and 10.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same forward TEA mask, backward single-gate T-MLP recurrence, and temporal enhancement in the first half of the blocks. Newly tested gate and width variants are ablation configurations, not replacements of the proposed method.

E1.justification: The static-image, neuromorphic, serialized-image, speech, and action-recognition benchmarks and four encoding schemes are retained. New analyses use existing datasets. SVHN and model-size evaluations were already present in v1's Appendix B.

E2.justification: The new gate comparison evaluates TEFormer-EMA and TEFormer-GRU against TEFormer. Table 9 adds efficiency comparisons with Spikformer, SDT, and TIM. Comparator membership in retained benchmark tables is unchanged; QKFormer is mentioned in the new efficiency prose but is absent from that table.

E3.justification: New evaluations vary the MLP ratio between 2 and 4 and the number of enhanced blocks from one to four within a fixed 4-block, 384-dimensional architecture. They introduce FLOPs, parameter counts, and estimated MAC/AC energy measures. Previously reported benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 7, 9, and 10 substantially extend design validation: they test single-gate versus GRU/EMA updates, the accuracy–cost tradeoff from reducing MLP width, and whether enhancing more layers helps. Existing module, direction, alpha, encoding, and appendix model-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The new tables retain point-estimate reporting without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing result tables retain their values, while new tables substantially expand quantitative evidence. Table 7 reports CIFAR10 accuracies of 96.05, 95.90, and 96.24 for EMA, GRU, and the proposed gate. Table 9 reports 5.18 versus 2.39 mJ for MLP ratios 4 versus 2. Table 10 adds depth-dependent outcomes, but its two-layer CIFAR10 value of 96.04 conflicts with the retained 96.24 elsewhere; this does not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The neuron, TEA, T-MLP, encoding, and attention formulations are unchanged, including Appendix A. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about bidirectional temporal fusion, parallel forward attention, backward gated MLP processing, and broad encoding-robust performance. The abstract's code statement adds access information rather than a scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of gate efficiency, width-dependent computational costs, and the nonmonotonic benefit of enhancing more layers. Section 7.3 newly restricts applicability to window-based recognition rather than strictly causal online inference. Existing software-only, classification-only, and encoding-standard limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the default MLP ratio as 4, documents variant parameter counts, and adds a code-availability link. The embedded link contains a duplicated https:// prefix. Training hardware and existing implementation disclosures are unchanged, and the new energy estimates lack detailed estimation assumptions.

R1.justification: v2 adds dataset-source citations to Krizhevsky, Netzer, Li, Orchard, and Sironi. The Spikingformer reference receives a publication/title update without changing its evaluated identity or scores. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier temporal-enhancement methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a fuller neuromorphic-results subsection, expands discussion of existing appendix results, and rewrites the encoding discussion. It introduces an efficiency/design/limitations section and acknowledgments and impact statements. Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned from a biological-pathway and module schematic into an explicit block-level architecture showing shallow temporal enhancement and deeper processing. Three new analysis tables are added, and existing tables are redistributed. Appendix Figure 2 and the appendix tables retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new gate and depth controls, quantified efficiency tradeoffs, more explicit architecture diagram, and causal-inference limitation improve the justification and interpretation of the unchanged method. However, Table 10 introduces an unexplained 96.04 versus 96.24 CIFAR10 discrepancy, the efficiency prose invokes QKFormer without tabulating it, and the code hyperlink is malformed. Energy-estimation details also remain limited. These weaknesses constrain the net improvement despite the useful additional evidence.
